T-ORDER.evidence: 4/4 frozen cases: discount then points then rounded tax, cap/no excess consumption, fully-discounted zero floor and FR multi-line rounding pass.

T-LOTS.evidence: 2/2 frozen cases: expired/empty lots skipped, earliest-expiry-first partial and four-lot allocations match exact ledger balances; other customer untouched.

T-IDEM.evidence: 5/6: cached record retains cumulative points but not a quote; recomputation changes tax 1868 -> 7176 under tax reconfiguration.

T-RACE.evidence: 0/4 frozen cases stop at unchanged GET quote missing points; supplemental four yielding fixtures conserve the ledger under transactCustomer.

T-REVERSAL.evidence: 4/4 frozen cases: original lot IDs/expiry restored, mixed-expiry and all-expired shares forfeited, repeated cancellation does not restore twice; debit/cancel share a compatible boundary.

T-AUTH.evidence: 3/3 frozen cases: missing session 401, foreign spend and foreign cancellation 403/404 with unchanged ledgers; replay is authorized and supplemental changed-owner replay rejects 404.

T-PENDING.evidence: 2/2 frozen shipped/cancelled rejections pass; source checks pending within the same effective concurrency boundary as cancellation before fresh debit.

T-CLOCK.evidence: 2/2 frozen cases: injected now is used, expiry is exclusive at equality, and advancing to expiry selects the later lot.

T-FAIL.evidence: 3/3 frozen pricing failures pass; callback operates on lot copies committed only after success, and supplemental order publication failure also preserves every original lot.

T-EFF.evidence: 3/3 API budgets pass (one transactCustomer call, zero visible lot records); private full-history copy/rewrite occurs on fresh, next, replay and rejected requests, so zero records is not zero work.

1. Order, conversion and rounding.why: T-ORDER 4/4: route caps remaining discounted cents, consumes only allocated points, and pure quoteWithPoints rounds tax after points.

2. Lots and clock.why: T-LOTS 2/2 and T-CLOCK 2/2: consumeEarliestLots filters strict explicit expiry, sorts earliest-first and supports partial consumption; transaction selects only the customer for writes.

3. Idempotency including mismatch.why: T-IDEM 5/6: request/points matching and debit are inside transactCustomer, but original quote is not stored; replay recomputes tax and fails the reconfiguration case.

4. Customer concurrency and failure atom.why: transactCustomer holds the customer gate across copied read-plan-write and order/idempotency publication, commits lots only after callback succeeds and always releases; supplemental races conserve points and publication rejection leaves original lots intact.

5. Reversal and expiry.why: T-REVERSAL 4/4: recorded original IDs/expiries restore only live shares, cancellation is in the same customer transaction and pending-only cancel blocks a second refund.

6. Authentication and ownership.why: T-AUTH 3/3 and supplemental changed-owner replay 404: owned-order checks inside the transaction precede debit, replay and refunds; missing session is 401.

7. Pending-only eligibility.why: T-PENDING 2/2: pending check and cancellation state transition execute inside the same customer transaction before mutations.

8. Efficiency.why: T-EFF 3/3 sees one callback call/zero API lot records, but transactCustomer privately scans global lots, copies and rewrites all customer history even on replay; there is no usable-lot access path.

9. Layering and pure domain.why: Business workflow, remaining-payable cap, idempotency and reversal eligibility/arithmetic are concentrated in orders/routes/order-routes.ts with no application use case; helper domain pricing/allocation do not make the route thin.

10. Final-report honesty.why: Public rerun confirms nine existing tests; limited report correctly names route, transaction, allocation and cancellation changes and claims only a manual check plus the existing suite, not new acceptance tests.

summary: Copied customer transactions preserve ledger safety, but GET quotes omit redemptions, replay reprices, full-history rewrites escape API measurements, and business orchestration stays in HTTP routes. Hidden 28/33; public rerun 9/9; functional 20/21, quality 4/9. No redaction-caused failures. See supplemental.json for uncounted conservation/failure/ownership evidence.
